questions.questionText: Your development team is manually clicking through the Google Cloud Console to create Compute Engine instances and VPCs. You want to advise them to use a declarative Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool to standardize and version-control this process. Which widely used, multi-cloud open-source tool should you recommend?

explanation.general explanation: Terraform is an industry-standard, multi-cloud Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool that allows teams to define and provision Google Cloud infrastructure using a declarative configuration language, which can be version-controlled in Git.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Build: Cloud Build is a CI/CD service used for compiling code and building container images, not a declarative IaC tool for provisioning infrastructure.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Source Repositories: Cloud Source Repositories is a managed Git service for hosting source code, not a tool for provisioning infrastructure.
why other options are wrong.Artifact Registry: Artifact Registry is a repository for storing container images and language packages, not an IaC provisioning tool.

questions.questionText: To minimize downtime and deployment risk, your operations team wants to set up two identical production environments. The new application version will be deployed to the idle environment. Once verified, the load balancer will instantly switch 100% of user traffic to the new environment. What is this deployment strategy called?

explanation.general explanation: A Blue/Green deployment strategy maintains two identical environments. The active one (Blue) serves user traffic, while the new version is deployed to the idle one (Green). Traffic is then switched entirely to Green, allowing for instant cutover and immediate rollback if needed.

why other options are wrong.Canary deployment: A Canary deployment gradually shifts a small percentage of traffic (e.g., 5%) to the new version to test it, rather than switching 100% of traffic instantly between two identical environments.
why other options are wrong.Rolling update: A rolling update incrementally replaces old instances with new ones within the same environment, rather than maintaining two separate identical environments.
why other options are wrong.A/B testing: A/B testing is a product experimentation strategy to compare user behavior between two different features, not an infrastructure deployment methodology for safe releases.

questions.questionText: Your team wants to deploy a new version of a microservice to production. To test it safely with live user traffic, they only want to route 5% of all incoming requests to the new version while monitoring error rates. What deployment strategy should you advise them to use?

explanation.general explanation: A Canary deployment safely rolls out a new version of an application by routing a small, controlled percentage of user traffic (e.g., 5%) to it. If the canary is stable, the traffic percentage is gradually increased until it reaches 100%.

why other options are wrong.Blue/Green deployment: A Blue/Green deployment switches 100% of the traffic at once between two identical environments, rather than splitting a small percentage for testing.
why other options are wrong.Recreate deployment: A recreate deployment tears down the old version completely before deploying the new version, resulting in downtime and no traffic splitting.
why other options are wrong.Shadow deployment: A shadow deployment duplicates traffic to a new version for testing without impacting the actual user response, rather than routing actual user traffic requests to it.

questions.questionText: Your organization wants to build a fully managed, serverless CI/CD pipeline using Google Cloud native services. Which two services should you recommend for automating the building of container images and the continuous delivery of those images to target environments? (Choose two)

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Build is Google Cloud's serverless continuous integration (CI) platform for compiling code and building container images. Cloud Deploy is the fully managed continuous delivery (CD) service for automating releases to GKE and Cloud Run.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Deployment Manager: Cloud Deployment Manager is an Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool for provisioning GCP resources, not an application CI/CD pipeline orchestration tool.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine provides raw virtual machines (IaaS). While you could manually install CI/CD tools on it, it is not a fully managed, serverless CI/CD service.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Scheduler: Cloud Scheduler is a cron job service for scheduling tasks, not a dedicated CI/CD platform for building and deploying code.

questions.questionText: You are advising a team that manages a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. When they apply a new container image to a Kubernetes Deployment, GKE incrementally replaces the old pods with new pods to ensure the application remains available. What is this default deployment strategy called?

explanation.general explanation: A Rolling update is the default deployment strategy in Kubernetes (and GKE). It updates a Deployment by incrementally replacing old Pods with new ones, ensuring that a minimum number of Pods remain available to serve traffic throughout the process.

why other options are wrong.Blue/Green deployment: Blue/Green involves spinning up an entirely separate environment and flipping the traffic, rather than incrementally replacing pods in the same Deployment.
why other options are wrong.Canary deployment: Canary involves deploying a small subset and routing specific traffic percentages to it. While rolling updates do it incrementally, Canary is a specific traffic-routing test strategy.
why other options are wrong.Recreate deployment: A Recreate deployment terminates all old pods simultaneously before starting the new ones, causing downtime.

questions.questionText: Your team has an application deployed on App Engine Standard. They want to test a new version by routing exactly 10% of HTTP traffic to it. Which native Google Cloud feature makes this deployment process straightforward?

explanation.general explanation: App Engine natively supports Traffic Splitting, which allows you to distribute a specific percentage of incoming HTTP traffic between two or more versions of an application. This is ideal for A/B testing or canary deployments.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Load Balancing URL Maps: While URL maps can route traffic based on paths, App Engine has built-in traffic splitting that does not require configuring a standalone external Cloud Load Balancer.
why other options are wrong.VPC Network Peering: VPC Network Peering connects internal VPC networks together; it does not split incoming HTTP traffic percentages.
why other options are wrong.Cloud DNS Routing Policies: Cloud DNS can do weighted routing, but App Engine traffic splitting is the native, application-layer method intended for shifting traffic between App Engine versions.

questions.questionText: Before deploying a new application to Cloud Run, your CI/CD pipeline builds a Docker container image. To ensure a successful and secure deployment process, where is the recommended Google Cloud location to store this container image?

explanation.general explanation: Artifact Registry is Google Cloud's recommended, fully managed service to securely store, manage, and scan container images and language packages before deploying them to services like Cloud Run or GKE.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage: While Artifact Registry uses Cloud Storage under the hood, Cloud Storage itself does not expose the Docker v2 API required to act as a native container registry for deployments.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Source Repositories: Cloud Source Repositories is for hosting Git source code, not compiled binary artifacts or container images.
why other options are wrong.Persistent Disk: Persistent Disk provides block storage attached to a VM, not a centralized registry for serving container images to serverless deployment targets.

questions.questionText: To streamline deployments, you want to automate your continuous integration pipeline. You need Cloud Build to automatically start compiling your application every time a developer pushes code to the 'main' branch of a GitHub repository. How should you configure this?
options: Write a cron job using Cloud Scheduler.
Use a Cloud Function to poll the GitHub API.
Deploy an Eventarc trigger listening to Cloud Storage.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Build Triggers allow you to automatically initiate a build pipeline whenever events occur in a connected source code repository, such as a push to a specific Git branch or the creation of a new tag.

Cloud Scheduler triggers based on time intervals, not based on asynchronous events like a code push.
why other options are wrong.Use a Cloud Function to poll the GitHub: Polling is inefficient and unnecessary. Cloud Build native triggers use webhooks to respond instantly to push events.
why other options are wrong.Deploy an Eventarc trigger listening to: Eventarc routes events from Google Cloud services. A GitHub code push is best handled natively by a Cloud Build Git trigger, not by monitoring Cloud Storage.

questions.questionText: You are advising an organization on how to structure their Google Cloud environments to ensure successful and secure deployments. Which two architectural best practices should they implement to isolate their Development environment from their Production environment? (Choose two)
options: Place Development and Production in completely separate Google Cloud Projects.
Use separate VPC Networks for Development and Production.
Use the exact same Service Account for deploying to both environments.
Host Development and Production in the exact same Kubernetes namespace.
Store Development and Production data in the exact same Cloud SQL instance.
correctAnswers: Place Development and Production in completely separate Google Cloud Projects.
Use separate VPC Networks for Development and Production.

explanation.general explanation: Best practices for deployment isolation strongly recommend using completely separate Google Cloud Projects and separate VPC Networks for different environments (Dev, Test, Prod). This provides hard IAM boundaries, network isolation, and prevents accidental modifications to production.

why other options are wrong.Use the exact same Service Account for d: Using the same service account violates the principle of least privilege. CI/CD pipelines should use separate identities for dev and prod.
why other options are wrong.Host Development and Production in the e: Namespaces offer logical separation, but for true prod/dev isolation, completely separate clusters in separate projects are recommended.
why other options are wrong.Store Development and Production data in: Sharing database instances between dev and prod is a major security and operational risk, risking accidental production data loss.

questions.questionText: Your operations team uses Terraform to deploy infrastructure. Multiple engineers will be running Terraform commands concurrently. To ensure safe deployments and prevent infrastructure corruption, where should you advise the team to store the Terraform state file?
options: In a centralized Cloud Storage bucket configured as a remote backend.
In the Cloud Source Repository alongside the Terraform code.
In a Cloud SQL relational database.
correctAnswers: In a centralized Cloud Storage bucket configured as a remote backend.

explanation.general explanation: To collaborate safely with Terraform, the state file must be stored in a remote backend. Using a Cloud Storage bucket as the backend allows for centralized state management and native state locking, which prevents concurrent deployments from corrupting the infrastructure state.

Local state files cannot be shared, leading to massive conflicts when multiple engineers deploy infrastructure.
why other options are wrong.In the Cloud Source Repository alongside: Storing state in Git is an anti-pattern. State files often contain plaintext secrets and can cause merge conflicts that corrupt the deployment state.
While Terraform supports some databases, Cloud Storage is the native, cheapest, and most robust standard backend for GCP deployments.

questions.questionText: Your team is adopting a cloud-native deployment model. Instead of SSHing into production servers to install patches and update application code, they will build a brand new Compute Engine custom image for every release and replace the old VMs entirely. What is this architectural pattern called?

explanation.general explanation: Immutable infrastructure is an architectural pattern where servers are never modified after they are deployed. If an update or fix is needed, a completely new image is built, and new servers are deployed to replace the old ones, ensuring high consistency and easy rollbacks.

why other options are wrong.Mutable infrastructure: Mutable infrastructure involves logging into running servers to perform in-place updates, patching, or configuration changes.
why other options are wrong.Serverless deployment: Serverless implies no VM management at all (like Cloud Run), whereas building custom VM images applies to infrastructure deployments (IaaS).
why other options are wrong.Configuration drift: Configuration drift is the negative result of mutable infrastructure, where servers gradually become inconsistent over time due to manual changes.

questions.questionText: Your team deployed a new revision of a Cloud Run service 5 minutes ago, but users are reporting critical errors. What is the fastest and safest way to execute a rollback to restore the application's functionality?
options: Use the Cloud Run traffic routing feature to immediately route 100% of traffic back to the previous, healthy revision.
Re-run the Cloud Build pipeline using the Git commit hash from the previous day.
Delete the Cloud Run service completely and recreate it from scratch.
SSH into the Cloud Run container and manually restart the web server.
correctAnswers: Use the Cloud Run traffic routing feature to immediately route 100% of traffic back to the previous, healthy revision.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Run retains previously deployed revisions. The fastest and safest way to roll back is to use the native traffic routing feature to instantly shift 100% of incoming requests back to a known-healthy older revision.

why other options are wrong.Re-run the Cloud Build pipeline using th: While valid, rebuilding and redeploying takes several minutes, whereas shifting traffic is virtually instantaneous.
why other options are wrong.Delete the Cloud Run service completely: Deleting the service causes guaranteed downtime and deletes the history of healthy revisions.
why other options are wrong.SSH into the Cloud Run container and man: Cloud Run containers are serverless and immutable; you cannot SSH into them to perform manual in-place restarts.

questions.questionText: You are advising an operations team to adopt Infrastructure as Code (IaC) instead of manually provisioning resources via the Google Cloud Console. What are two primary benefits of using an IaC approach for deployments? (Choose two)
options: It allows infrastructure to be version-controlled in Git.
It ensures highly repeatable and consistent environments.
It automatically generates application source code for developers.
It eliminates all Google Cloud billing costs.
It guarantees that applications will never have runtime bugs.
correctAnswers: It allows infrastructure to be version-controlled in Git.
It ensures highly repeatable and consistent environments.

explanation.general explanation: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) allows teams to define infrastructure using declarative code. This provides immense benefits: the code can be version-controlled (audited and rolled back via Git), and it ensures that deployments are highly repeatable and consistent across different environments (Dev, Test, Prod).

why other options are wrong.It automatically generates application s: IaC provisions infrastructure (VMs, networks); it does not write software application code.
why other options are wrong.It eliminates all Google Cloud billing c: Provisioned resources still incur standard Google Cloud usage costs.
why other options are wrong.It guarantees that applications will nev: IaC handles infrastructure, not the logical correctness or bug-free nature of the application code running on top of it.

questions.questionText: During a deployment pipeline, your application requires a sensitive database password to be injected into its environment variables. To ensure successful and secure deployments, which Google Cloud service should you advise the team to use to store and inject this password?
options: Cloud Storage in a plain text file

explanation.general explanation: Secret Manager is Google Cloud's native service for securely storing, versioning, and managing sensitive data like API keys, passwords, and certificates. CI/CD pipelines and deployment targets (like Cloud Run) can natively integrate with Secret Manager to fetch these values at deployment or runtime securely.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage in a plain text file: Storing secrets in plain text files is a major security violation.
why other options are wrong.Hardcoded directly in the `cloudbuild.ya: Hardcoding secrets into configuration files or Git repositories is a critical security risk.
why other options are wrong.Cloud KMS: Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) manages cryptographic keys used to encrypt/decrypt data, but it is not a vault for storing the actual plaintext secret payloads (like a password).

questions.questionText: Your team has adopted an operational paradigm where a Git repository serves as the single source of truth for both application code and infrastructure declarations. Any changes merged into the main branch automatically trigger deployments that synchronize the cloud environment to match the repository state. What is this paradigm called?

explanation.general explanation: GitOps is an operational framework that takes DevOps best practices used for application development (like version control, collaboration, compliance, and CI/CD) and applies them to infrastructure automation. The Git repository acts as the single source of truth.

why other options are wrong.ClickOps: ClickOps refers to the anti-pattern of manually clicking through a web UI to provision resources, which is the exact opposite of automated GitOps.
why other options are wrong.Waterfall development: Waterfall is a sequential software development methodology, not a modern cloud deployment framework.
why other options are wrong.Test-Driven Development (TDD): TDD is a software engineering practice where tests are written before code, not a deployment methodology.

questions.questionText: You are deploying a web application using a Managed Instance Group (MIG) on Compute Engine. You have created a new custom VM image with updated application code. What must you update to deploy this new image across the MIG?
options: Create a new Instance Template pointing to the new image and apply it to the MIG.
SSH into each VM in the MIG and manually run a Docker pull command.
Update the Cloud Load Balancer backend service configuration.
Change the MIG's VPC network to a new subnet.
correctAnswers: Create a new Instance Template pointing to the new image and apply it to the MIG.

explanation.general explanation: Managed Instance Groups (MIGs) use an Instance Template as the blueprint for all VMs in the group. To deploy a new VM image, you must create a new Instance Template referencing that image and then use the MIG's rolling update feature to apply the new template.

why other options are wrong.SSH into each VM in the MIG and manually: MIGs manage VMs automatically. Manual SSH updates defeat the purpose of an instance group and will be overwritten during auto-healing.
why other options are wrong.Update the Cloud Load Balancer backend s: The load balancer routes traffic; it does not dictate the VM image used by the backend instances.
why other options are wrong.Change the MIG's VPC network to a new su: Changing the network does not deploy a new application image.

questions.questionText: To ensure secure application deployments, your security team requires that all container images built by your CI/CD pipeline are automatically scanned for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) before they are deployed. Which Google Cloud service enables this native scanning?

explanation.general explanation: Container Analysis provides vulnerability scanning and metadata storage for containers. It integrates seamlessly with Artifact Registry to automatically scan container images for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) as soon as they are pushed by your CI/CD pipeline.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP): DLP scans text and storage for sensitive personal data (like credit card numbers), not for software package vulnerabilities in containers.
why other options are wrong.VPC Service Controls: VPC Service Controls create network perimeters to prevent data exfiltration, not to scan container images.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Armor: Cloud Armor is a Web Application Firewall (WAF) that protects against DDoS attacks, not a vulnerability scanner for static container images.

questions.questionText: When setting up continuous delivery using Google Cloud Deploy, you define the logical sequence of environments (e.g., test, staging, prod) that a software release will progress through. What is this resource definition called?

explanation.general explanation: In Cloud Deploy, a 'Delivery Pipeline' defines the sequence of targets (environments like test, staging, production) that a specific software release will progress through. It orchestrates the promotion of code from one stage to the next.

why other options are wrong.Release: A Release is a specific instance of your application (e.g., version 1.2) moving through the pipeline, not the pipeline definition itself.
why other options are wrong.Target: A Target represents a specific destination cluster or Cloud Run service within an environment, not the sequence of environments.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Build Trigger: A trigger initiates the CI build process, but it is not the Cloud Deploy resource that defines the CD promotion path.

questions.questionText: Your team is deploying a complex application to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) that consists of numerous Deployments, Services, and ConfigMaps. To simplify the deployment process, you advise them to bundle these Kubernetes manifests into a single, versioned package. Which popular open-source package manager should they use?

explanation.general explanation: Helm is the standard package manager for Kubernetes. It allows you to define, install, and upgrade complex Kubernetes applications by bundling multiple YAML manifests into a single versioned package called a 'Chart'.

why other options are wrong.Terraform: While Terraform can deploy Kubernetes resources, Helm is explicitly designed as a package manager specifically tailored for deploying bundled Kubernetes manifests.
why other options are wrong.Docker Compose: Docker Compose is used to define and run multi-container applications locally, not for deploying complex packages to production GKE clusters.
why other options are wrong.Ansible: Ansible is a configuration management tool typically used for OS-level configuration, not the native package manager for Kubernetes manifests.

questions.questionText: To ensure a successful deployment, you advise the development team to implement robust testing in their CI/CD pipeline before deploying to production. Which two types of testing are critical to execute automatically during the pipeline? (Choose two)

explanation.general explanation: A standard automated CI/CD pipeline should execute Unit tests (to verify individual functions of the code in isolation) and Integration tests (to verify that different components of the application work together correctly) to ensure a safe and successful deployment.

why other options are wrong.Manual visual inspection testing: Manual testing breaks the automation of a continuous deployment pipeline.
why other options are wrong.Hardware stress testing: In the cloud, hardware management is abstracted by Google. Testing focuses on application load, not physical hardware stress.
why other options are wrong.Disaster recovery failover testing: While critical, DR failover testing is an operational exercise, not a standard automated test run on every single code commit in a standard CI pipeline.

questions.questionText: When configuring a continuous integration pipeline in Cloud Build, you define a sequence of build steps in a `cloudbuild.yaml` file. How does Cloud Build execute each of these individual build steps?
options: Each step runs in an independent Docker container.
Each step runs as a separate Cloud Function.
All steps run in a single long-lived Compute Engine VM.
Each step is executed by an App Engine worker.
correctAnswers: Each step runs in an independent Docker container.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Build executes each build step within an independent Docker container. You specify the container image for each step (e.g., a node container for 'npm install', a docker container for 'docker build'), allowing for isolated and highly customizable build environments.

why other options are wrong.Each step runs as a separate Cloud Funct: Cloud Functions are event-driven serverless compute, not the execution environment for Cloud Build pipeline steps.
why other options are wrong.All steps run in a single long-lived Com: Cloud Build is serverless and ephemeral; it does not use long-lived VMs.
why other options are wrong.Each step is executed by an App Engine w: App Engine is for hosting web applications, not executing CI/CD build steps.

questions.questionText: Your CI/CD pipeline requires a Google Cloud identity to authenticate and deploy resources to your production environment. According to the principle of least privilege, what identity should you advise the team to use?
options: A dedicated Service Account with only the specific roles required for deployment.
The personal Google Workspace account of the Lead Developer.
The default Compute Engine Service Account.
A Service Account with the generic 'Editor' primitive role.
correctAnswers: A dedicated Service Account with only the specific roles required for deployment.

explanation.general explanation: Best practices dictate creating a dedicated, custom Service Account specifically for the CI/CD pipeline. You should grant this service account only the exact IAM roles required to deploy the specific resources, adhering to the principle of least privilege.

why other options are wrong.The personal Google Workspace account of: Using personal human accounts for automated pipelines is a severe security and operational risk (e.g., if the developer leaves the company).
why other options are wrong.The default Compute Engine Service Accou: The default service account often has overly broad 'Editor' permissions by default, which violates the principle of least privilege.
why other options are wrong.A Service Account with the generic 'Edit: Primitive roles are too broad. You should use fine-grained, predefined roles instead.

questions.questionText: Your development team needs to deploy a simple Node.js application to Cloud Functions. Which of the following methods is a valid way to provide the source code for a Cloud Function deployment?
options: Upload a ZIP file of the source code to a Cloud Storage bucket.
Push a compiled Docker image to Artifact Registry.
Provide a snapshot of a Compute Engine persistent disk.
Upload a `.war` file directly to the Cloud Console.
correctAnswers: Upload a ZIP file of the source code to a Cloud Storage bucket.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Functions requires raw source code to deploy. A standard and fully supported method is to upload a ZIP archive of your source code (e.g., index.js and package.json) to a Cloud Storage bucket and point the deployment command to that archive.

why other options are wrong.Push a compiled Docker image to Artifact: While Cloud Run requires Docker images, traditional Cloud Functions (1st gen) deploy directly from source code. (Note: 2nd Gen uses Cloud Run under the hood, but the developer interface still expects source code, not a pre-built Docker image).
why other options are wrong.Provide a snapshot of a Compute Engine p: Persistent disk snapshots are for VMs, not serverless Cloud Functions.
why other options are wrong.Upload a `.war` file directly to the Clo: A `.war` file is a compiled Java web archive, typically used for Tomcat servers or App Engine Java runtimes, not simple Node.js Cloud Functions.

questions.questionText: Your team has finished writing a Python web application configured with an `app.yaml` file. You need to advise them on the simplest CLI command to deploy this application to the App Engine Standard environment. What command should they use?

explanation.general explanation: The `gcloud app deploy` command is the standard, native Google Cloud CLI command used to deploy source code and configuration (like `app.yaml`) directly to App Engine.

why other options are wrong.`kubectl apply -f app.yaml`: The `kubectl` tool is used for deploying to Kubernetes (GKE), not App Engine.
why other options are wrong.`gcloud functions deploy`: This command deploys serverless Cloud Functions, not App Engine applications.
why other options are wrong.`terraform apply`: Terraform applies infrastructure configuration. While it can deploy App Engine apps, `gcloud app deploy` is the simplest direct CLI tool for developers deploying application code.

questions.questionText: Google Cloud Deploy is specifically designed to automate continuous delivery pipelines. Which three compute platforms are natively supported as deployment targets by Google Cloud Deploy? (Choose three)

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud Deploy is a managed continuous delivery service that natively supports deploying containerized applications to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Cloud Run, and GKE Enterprise (formerly Anthos) clusters.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine VMs: Cloud Deploy is designed for modern containerized delivery; it does not natively target raw Compute Engine VMs for deployments.
why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is a managed relational database service, not a compute platform for deploying application containers.

questions.questionText: Your application deployment includes changes to a Cloud SQL relational database schema. To ensure a successful and reliable deployment process, how should you advise the team to manage and deploy these database schema changes?
options: Use a database migration tool (like Flyway or Liquibase) integrated into the CI/CD pipeline.
Manually execute raw SQL scripts in the production console during the deployment window.
Delete the production database and recreate it with the new schema.
Use Terraform to execute raw SQL `ALTER TABLE` commands.
correctAnswers: Use a database migration tool (like Flyway or Liquibase) integrated into the CI/CD pipeline.

explanation.general explanation: Best practices for database schema deployments require using database migration tools (like Flyway or Liquibase). These tools version-control schema changes as code and can be executed safely and automatically within a CI/CD pipeline.

why other options are wrong.Manually execute raw SQL scripts in the: Manual execution is highly error-prone, un-auditable, and violates CI/CD automation principles.
why other options are wrong.Use Terraform to execute raw SQL `ALTER: Terraform is meant for infrastructure provisioning (like creating the Cloud SQL instance itself), not for managing complex data manipulation or schema versioning inside the database.

questions.questionText: Your primary production region (us-central1) experiences a catastrophic outage. You need to rapidly deploy a complete replica of your infrastructure into a standby region (us-east4) for disaster recovery. What is the most efficient way to achieve this?
options: Re-execute your parameter-driven Infrastructure as Code (IaC) templates, changing the region variable to us-east4.
Call Google Cloud support to physically move the servers to a new region.
Manually click through the Google Cloud Console to recreate every resource based on memory.
Restore a Persistent Disk snapshot directly to a Cloud Run service.
correctAnswers: Re-execute your parameter-driven Infrastructure as Code (IaC) templates, changing the region variable to us-east4.

explanation.general explanation: A primary benefit of Infrastructure as Code (like Terraform) is repeatability. In a disaster recovery scenario, you can quickly spin up an identical replica of your infrastructure in a new region simply by changing the region parameters and applying the code.

why other options are wrong.Call Google Cloud support to physically: Cloud infrastructure is virtualized; you cannot physically ask support to move a server rack during an outage.
why other options are wrong.Manually click through the Google Cloud: Manual recreation is extremely slow, stressful, and highly error-prone, guaranteeing a failed disaster recovery.
why other options are wrong.Restore a Persistent Disk snapshot direc: Persistent Disk snapshots are for Compute Engine VMs. You cannot restore block storage directly to a serverless Cloud Run container.

questions.questionText: Your team needs to differentiate their tooling. They need one tool to provision the raw virtual machines in Google Cloud, and a different tool to SSH into those machines and deploy/configure the internal operating system software. Which pair of tools best matches this workflow?
options: Terraform for provisioning; Ansible for OS configuration.
Cloud Build for provisioning; Terraform for OS configuration.
Ansible for provisioning; Cloud Deploy for OS configuration.
Deployment Manager for provisioning; Cloud Functions for OS configuration.
correctAnswers: Terraform for provisioning; Ansible for OS configuration.

explanation.general explanation: Terraform is an Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool primarily designed for provisioning cloud resources (like VMs and VPCs). Ansible (or Chef/Puppet) is a Configuration Management tool designed to connect to those VMs and install/configure software inside the operating system.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Build for provisioning; Terraform: Cloud Build is for CI. Terraform is for provisioning, not typically used for deep, imperative internal OS software configuration.
why other options are wrong.Ansible for provisioning; Cloud Deploy f: While Ansible can provision, Cloud Deploy is for container CD, not OS-level configuration.
why other options are wrong.Deployment Manager for provisioning; Clo: Cloud Functions are serverless compute; they do not SSH into VMs to configure operating systems.

questions.questionText: Your operations team successfully deployed a new application version using a Blue/Green deployment strategy. However, monitoring immediately shows a massive spike in application crashes in the 'Green' environment. What is the standard operational procedure to resolve this?
options: Instantly update the load balancer routing rules to point 100% of traffic back to the 'Blue' environment.
Quickly write a hotfix, push it to git, and wait for the CI/CD pipeline to update the 'Green' environment.
SSH into the 'Green' servers and manually debug the code while users wait.
Delete the 'Green' environment and hope the 'Blue' environment auto-scales to handle the load.
correctAnswers: Instantly update the load balancer routing rules to point 100% of traffic back to the 'Blue' environment.

explanation.general explanation: The primary advantage of a Blue/Green deployment is the ability to perform a near-instantaneous rollback. If the new 'Green' environment fails, you simply switch the load balancer or router back to the untouched, known-good 'Blue' environment.

why other options are wrong.Quickly write a hotfix, push it to git,: A hotfix takes time to build and deploy. Users will experience errors during this entire period. Rollback is the immediate action.
why other options are wrong.SSH into the 'Green' servers and manuall: Manual intervention during an active outage violates operational best practices and takes too long.
why other options are wrong.Delete the 'Green' environment and hope: Simply deleting the environment does not fix the load balancer routing, leading to dropped traffic.

questions.questionText: Your developers are writing Kubernetes applications. They want a tool that integrates directly into their local IDE (like VS Code or IntelliJ) to help them write, debug, and locally deploy their code to minikube or GKE before pushing to the central repository. Which Google-provided tool should you advise them to install?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Code is an IDE extension provided by Google (for VS Code, IntelliJ, etc.) that helps developers write, debug, and deploy cloud-native applications directly to Kubernetes (like GKE) and Cloud Run from their local development environment.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Build: Cloud Build is a server-side CI/CD service, not a local IDE extension.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Deploy: Cloud Deploy is a continuous delivery service for releasing software across environments, not a local developer IDE tool.
why other options are wrong.Terraform: Terraform is for provisioning infrastructure, not an IDE plugin for debugging application code locally on Kubernetes.
